summary.intent: Execute Phase 60 (IPNS Verification Cross-Layer Closeout) using wave-based parallel execution to harden IPNS verification across Rust and TypeScript layers, making all resolve paths strictly fail-closed.
summary.outcome: Wave 1 completed successfully (plans 60-01, 60-02, 60-03) and Wave 2 started (60-04 in progress). All three Wave 1 crates compile clean with 251/251 sdk-core tests passing. Wave 2 was cut off mid-execution in the transcript.

repo: Phase 60 has 8 plans across 4 waves; Wave 4 (60-08) is non-autonomous and requires a human-action checkpoint for staging wipe + redeploy + smoke-test.

The IPNS verify chokepoint was originally split across crates (crates/fuse/src/verify.rs) but was consolidated into crates/api-client/src/ipns.rs in 60-01 so sdk/fuse/desktop share one implementation.
All 9 first-publish IPNS producers previously used seq=0; 60-02 unified them to seq=1 as a precondition for the strict resolve verifier.

The VerifyError::Legacy variant was fully removed in 60-01 — all 9 FUSE caller arms folded to use Invalid instead, despite 60-04 being the declared scope for that work (compile necessity forced it early).
Pre-existing vendored fuser dead-code warnings are expected and benign; do not treat them as regressions.
No project-specific executor skills (gsd-tools query init.execute-phase returned empty payload).
No submodules in this repo — all plans use worktree isolation per config.

code.finding: Was the last remaining VerifyError::Legacy reference; folded to Invalid by 60-01 executor as a compile necessity, not 60-04 as planned.
Had a stale seq expectation of 0n that needed updating to 1n after 60-02 unified first-publish producers to seq=1.

workflow: The GSD harness worktree isolation mode (isolation='worktree') is unreliable for merge-back in this setup — the orchestrator cannot access the worktree path/branch manifest, so sequential subagents on the feature branch were used instead.
Mid-edit compiler diagnostics captured by an executor can be stale snapshots; always re-run cargo check authoritatively before marking a plan blocked.
Wave-level build/test gates (cargo check + full test suite) are essential for catching cross-plan integration issues before proceeding to the next wave.
60-03 executor proactively fixed a downstream test regression caused by 60-02 (vault.test.ts 0n→1n), which is a valid Rule 1 deviation when the fix is in scope and unambiguous.

friction: The execute-phase workflow required multiple sequential file reads (3 separate reads of execute-phase.md plus the worktree-gate and post-merge-gate step files) before any dispatch could happen, adding latency to phase startup.

The 60-01 executor reported a false compile error (metadata.rs:619 VerifyError::Legacy) mid-execution — it was a stale snapshot, not a real failure, but required an extra verification round-trip with grep + cargo check.

The worktree-based parallel execution mode (the workflow's primary performance path) was abandoned because the harness cannot reliably retrieve worktree branch names for merge-back, forcing sequential execution and higher wall-clock time.
Plan scope boundaries were crossed: 60-01 folded all FUSE Legacy caller arms (declared scope of 60-04) because the compiler forced it — creates ambiguity about what 60-04 still needs to do.
open_items: Wave 2 was in-flight (60-04 executing) when the transcript ended — 5 plans remain: 60-04, 60-05, 60-07 (Wave 2), 60-06 (Wave 3), 60-08 (Wave 4).
60-08 is a non-autonomous human checkpoint (staging wipe + redeploy + smoke-test for D-01/D-12 operational cutover) — requires manual action when reached.
60-04 scope needs re-evaluation since 60-01 already folded the 9 FUSE Legacy arms; the remaining work is 2 crates/sdk raw-resolve bypasses and 6 desktop Tauri resolve_ipns sites.
Windows WinFSP site coverage for seq=1 changes (60-02) is CI-gated only — no local verification possible.
The worktree merge-back limitation in the GSD harness should be investigated as a longer-term improvement to enable true parallel wave execution.
